In the [[mathematics|mathematical branch]] of [[topology]], a '''hyperspace''' (or a space equipped with a hypertopology) is a [[topological space]], which consists of the set ''CL(X)'' of all non-empty [[Closed set|closed]] subsets of another topological space ''X'', equipped with a topology so that the [[canonical map]]

<math>i : x \mapsto \overline{\{x\}},</math>

is a [[homeomorphism]] onto its image. As a consequence, a copy of the original space ''X'' lives inside its hyperspace ''CL(X)''.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Lucchetti|first=Roberto|author2=Angela Pasquale|title=A New Approach to a Hyperspace Theory|journal=Journal of Convex Analysis|year=1994|volume=1|issue=2|pages=173–193|url=http://www.heldermann-verlag.de/jca/jca01/jca01013.pdf|accessdate=20 January 2013}}</ref>  
<ref>{{cite book|last=Beer|first=G.|title=Topologies on closed and closed convex sets|year=1994|publisher=[[Kluwer Academic Publishers]]}}</ref>

Early examples of hypertopology include the [[Hausdorff distance|Hausdorff metric]]<ref>{{cite book|last=Hausdorff|first=F.|title=Mengenlehre|year=1927|publisher=W. de Gruyter|location=Berlin and Leipzig}}</ref> and [[#Vietoris topology|Vietoris topology]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Vietoris|first=L.|title=Stetige Mengen|journal=Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik|year=1921|volume=31|pages=173–204|doi=10.1007/BF01702717}}</ref>

==Notation==

Various notation is used by different authors to denote the set of all closed subsets of a topological space ''X'', including ''CL(X)'', <math>\mathcal{F}(X)</math> and <math> 2^X </math>.

==Examples==
===Vietoris topology===
Let <math>F</math> be a closed subset and <math>U_1,\ldots,U_n</math> be a finite collection of open subsets of ''X''.  Define

<math>
V(F,U_1,\ldots,U_n) = \{ Y \subseteq X \text{ closed} \mid
Y \cap F = \emptyset \text{ and } Y\cap U_i \neq \emptyset \text{ for every }1\leq i\leq n \}.
</math>

These sets form a basis for a topology on ''CL(X)'', called the Vietoris or finite topology, named for [[Leopold Vietoris]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Vietoris|first=L.|title=Stetige Mengen|journal=Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik|year=1921|volume=31|pages=173–204|doi=10.1007/BF01702717}}</ref>

===Fell topology===
A variant on the Vietoris topology is to allow only the sets <math>V(C,U_1,\ldots,U_n)</math> where ''C'' is a [[Compact space|compact subset]] of ''X'' and <math>U_1,\ldots,U_n</math> a finite collection of open subsets.  This is again a base for a topology on ''CL(X)'' called the Fell topology or the ''H''-topology.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fell |first1=J. M. G. |title=A Hausdorff topology for the closed subsets of a locally compact non- Hausdorff space |journal=Proc. Am. Math. Soc. |date=1962 |volume=13 |pages=472–476}}</ref>  Note, though, that the canonical map <math>i:x \mapsto \overline{\{x\}}</math> is a homeomorphism onto its image if and only if ''X'' is Hausdorff,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fell |first1=J. M. G. |title=A Hausdorff topology for the closed subsets of a locally compact non- Hausdorff space |journal=Proc. Am. Math. Soc. |date=1962 |volume=13 |pages=472–476}}</ref> so for non-Hausdorff ''X'', the Fell topology is not a hypertopology in the sense of this article.

The Vietoris and Fell topologies coincide if ''X'' is a compact space, but have quite different properties if not.  For instance, the Fell topology is always compact and it is compact Hausdorff whenever if ''X'' is locally compact.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fell |first1=J. M. G. |title=A Hausdorff topology for the closed subsets of a locally compact non- Hausdorff space |journal=Proc. Am. Math. Soc. |date=1962 |volume=13 |pages=472–476}}</ref>  On the other hand, the Vietoris topology is compact if and only if ''X'' is compact and Hausdorff if and only if ''X'' is [[regular space|regular]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Michael |first1=Ernest |title=Topologies on spaces of subsets |journal=Trans. Am. Math. Soc. |date=1951 |volume=71 |pages=152–182}}</ref>

===Other constructions===
The [[Hausdorff distance]] on the closed subsets of a bounded metric space ''X'' induces a topology on ''CL(X)''.  If ''X'' is a compact [[metric space]], this agrees with the Vietoris and Fell topologies.

The [[Chabauty topology]] on the closed subsets of a [[locally compact group]] coincides with the Fell topology.
